scope: Six-chapter pilot plus retained Mind page: Pāli 1–43, 100–115, 157–166, 221–234, and 290–305, in Pāli order
editorial_policy: T210 is preferred. Actual T212 or T213 historical counterparts are used only where the selected table has no T210 counterpart, and each reading retains its exact Taishō collection reference. Missing coverage is not filled by retranslating Pāli.

sources.title: Pāli–Chinese Dhammapada correspondence tables, chapters 1–3, 8, 12, 17, and 21
sources.note: Only correspondence facts and ancient verse quotations are retained; modern Pāli translations and explanatory commentary are not reproduced.

pinyin.method: pypinyin 0.55.0 citation-tone output, with manual contextual corrections for polyphonic and historical characters. Syllables are spaced character by character; word segmentation and tone sandhi are not asserted. New selection: contextual readings include 惓 juàn in 不惓, 長 zhǎng in 長老, 著 zhuó in 不著名色, 率 shuài in 率君二臣, 盡 jìn, 種 zhòng when planting and zhǒng for seed, 應 yìng in 能應, and 樂 yuè in 伎樂.
pinyin.status: editorial reading aid; not an independently reviewed historical pronunciation or translation

verses.note: T210 has no counterpart identified in the table. The displayed reading is from T212; its first phrase is 人若罵我 in CBETA, whereas the table quotes 若人罵我.
The table lists T213 14.10 for both Pāli 3 and 4. The Chinese verse is not an exact positive/negative pair like the Pāli; its relation is a qualified parallel.

edition_difference.table: 慍於怨者未嘗無怨不慍自除是道可宗
edition_difference.cbeta: 慍於怨者未甞無怨不慍自除是道可宗

verses.note: Ken Su identifies this T210 counterpart, but its admonition to examine oneself differs from the Pāli wording. Alignment is by verse, not literal phrase.

edition_difference.table: 以真為偽以真為偽是為邪計不得真利
edition_difference.cbeta: 以真為偽以偽為真是為邪計不得真利

verses.note: The correspondence table repeats 以真為偽 in its second clause. The display follows CBETA: 以真為偽、以偽為真.

edition_difference.table: 發行不放逸約以自調心慧能作錠明不返冥淵中
edition_difference.cbeta: 發行不放逸約以自調心慧能作定明不返冥淵中

verses.note: The table quotes 錠明; this CBETA edition reads 定明. That Chinese lamp/illumination wording differs from the Pāli island image; no harmonization is made.

Ken Su's verse division groups six clauses here; CBETA punctuation places a full stop after 去危為即安 and continues the final two clauses before the next mapped verse. This grouping follows the correspondence table, with CBETA punctuation retained.

edition_difference.table: 不自放逸從是多悟羸馬比良棄惡為賢
edition_difference.cbeta: 不自放恣從是多寤羸馬比良棄惡為賢

readings.note: An additional counterpart in Ken Su's table; the first listed reading (T210 31.17) retains the horse image more closely.

verses.note: Ken Su lists two T210 counterparts. T210 31.17 is selected first because it retains the horse comparison. The display preserves CBETA 放恣 and 寤, against the table's 放逸 and 悟. Verse numbers follow the correspondence table; CBETA does not assign those local verse numbers.
T210 has no counterpart identified in the table. This is T213 4.24: it preserves praise of heedfulness and criticism of heedlessness but omits the Pāli reference to Maghavā/Indra.

edition_difference.table: 比丘謹慎樂放逸多憂愆變諍小致大積惡入火焰
edition_difference.cbeta: 比丘謹慎樂放逸多憂𠎝變諍小致大積惡入火焰

verses.note: The Chinese counterpart differs substantially in its fire image: T210 speaks of accumulated evil entering fire, while the Pāli heedful monk burns fetters. CBETA's historical character 𠎝 is retained; Mandarin qiān corresponds to 愆.
T210 has no counterpart identified in the table. The displayed T213 4.32 is an actual historical Chinese verse, not a new translation of the Pāli.

edition_difference.table: 意使作笱難護難禁慧正其本其明乃大
edition_difference.cbeta: 意使作㺃難護難禁慧正其本其明乃大

verses.note: CBETA reads 意使作㺃; the correspondence table prints 笱. The historical character 㺃 is retained (modern Mandarin gǒu). The phrase is textually difficult; its interpretation is not resolved here.
T210 has no counterpart identified in the table. The displayed verse is T212 32.2.
The historical Chinese verse praises merit restraining evil, whereas the Pāli refers to one who has abandoned merit and demerit. Both wordings are preserved.
The Chinese opening uses a tortoise and the six faculties, rather than the Pāli body-as-pot image. The remaining fortress and Māra imagery supports the table's partial correspondence.
No counterpart is listed for Pāli 42 in T210, T212, or T213 in the selected scholarly correspondence table. This is not a claim that no Chinese parallel exists anywhere.

edition_difference.table: 雖誦千章不義何益不如一義聞行可度
edition_difference.cbeta: 雖誦千言不義何益不如一義聞行可度

verses.note: The T210 counterpart contrasts prolonged ritual offering with a moment of one-pointed recollection of Dharma; the Pāli speaks of honoring a developed person. Both historical formulations are retained.
The Chinese verse refers to honoring the Three Honored Ones (三尊), where Pāli speaks of honoring one who has developed himself.
The Pāli refers to seeing arising and passing away. T210 uses 成敗 and 見微知所忌; its wording is retained without harmonization.

edition_difference.table: 若人壽百歲不知大道義不如生一日學惟佛法要
edition_difference.cbeta: 若人壽百歲不知大道義不如生一日學推佛法要

verses.note: The correspondence table quotes 學惟佛法要. This pinned CBETA edition reads 學推佛法要; the display preserves that source reading.

edition_difference.table: 自愛身者慎護所守希望欲解學正不寐
edition_difference.cbeta: 自愛身者慎護所守悕望欲解學正不寐

readings.note: Additional historical counterpart identified by Ken Su; the first reading is displayed.

verses.note: T210 20.1 is displayed. Ken Su also identifies T210 30.12, which adds a frontier-city and hell image. The first Chinese reading does not reproduce the Pāli three watches of the night.

edition_difference.table: 身為第一常自勉學利乃誨人不惓則智
edition_difference.cbeta: 為身第一常自勉學利乃誨人不惓則智

verses.note: The Pāli makes oneself one’s refuge. T210 instead asks how a person unable to benefit himself can benefit others, then praises a well-trained mind and body. This is a qualified historical correspondence.
T210 preserves the creeper image but develops it as unchecked misconduct and desire; it does not reproduce the whole tree-and-enemy simile of Pāli.
The Chinese ending uses bitter seed rather than the Pāli bamboo/reed image. Its historical wording is retained.

The Pāli warns against neglecting one’s own welfare for another’s. T210 speaks of benefiting oneself and others without loss, and emphasizes discipline and learning. This is a substantial recensional difference.

edition_difference.table: 捨恚離慢避諸愛貪不著名色無為滅苦
edition_difference.cbeta: 捨恚離慢避諸愛會不著名色無為滅苦

verses.note: This pinned CBETA edition reads 避諸愛會 where the correspondence table quotes 避諸愛貪. The source spelling is preserved.
The Chinese charioteer simile ends with leaving darkness for light; the Pāli contrasts a true charioteer with others who merely hold reins.
T210 says not to demand much where Pāli urges giving when asked even if one has little. The rest of the truthfulness, non-anger, and heaven sequence supports the qualified correspondence.

verses.note: Ken Su lists both T210 7.1 and 25.6. The first is displayed because its deathless destination is closer to the Pāli; the second speaks of birth in heaven.

edition_difference.table: 意常覺悟明暮勤學漏盡意解可致泥洹
edition_difference.cbeta: 意常覺寤明慕勤學漏盡意解可致泥洹

readings.note: Additional historical counterpart identified by Ken Su; the first reading is displayed.

verses.note: Ken Su lists both T210 6.9 and 25.7. Both actual Chinese readings are retained; the first is displayed.

edition_difference.table: 人相謗毀自古至今既毀多言又毀訥訒亦毀中和世無不毀
edition_difference.cbeta: 人相謗毀自古至今既毀多言又毀訥忍亦毀中和世無不毀

verses.note: T210 treats praise and blame in terms of advantage and reputation; the Pāli says no one has ever been wholly praised or wholly blamed. This is a qualified correspondence.

edition_difference.table: 如羅漢淨莫而誣謗諸天咨嗟梵釋所稱
edition_difference.cbeta: 如羅漢淨莫而誣謗諸人咨嗟梵釋所稱

verses.note: T210 retains praise by Brahmā/Śakra but does not reproduce the Pāli gold-ornament simile. This pinned CBETA edition reads 諸人咨嗟, where the correspondence table quotes 諸天咨嗟.

edition_difference.table: 常守慎心以護瞋恚除意惡念思惟念道
edition_difference.cbeta: 常守慎心以護瞋恚除心惡念思惟念道

verses.note: T210 contrasts a small gift of peace with its greater reward, where Pāli contrasts giving up lesser happiness for greater happiness. The historical difference is preserved.
The Chinese verse contrasts diligent practice with doing what should not be done. It does not reproduce Pāli’s explicit mindfulness-of-the-body phrase.
The mother, ruler, ministers, and retinue imagery differs from the Pāli mother, father, kings, kingdom, and attendants sequence. No explanatory allegory is added to the verse.
No counterpart is listed in T210, T212, or T213 in the consulted correspondence table. This records the scope of this comparison, not absence throughout Chinese Buddhist literature.
